title: Rational Verdier duality on a smooth curve over a perfect field
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Put $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $C$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ be a dense open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$ its reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] closed complement [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work in the common finite-coefficient-field categories $D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], for $T=C,U,Z$; they are identified with the categories of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] on these schemes by the canonical exact $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linear equivalence $J_T$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], which also identifies the two categories of Weil pairs. For the structure morphism $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, put $\omega_T=Ra_T^!\Lambda$ as in [def-pur-conventions] and $D_T(-)=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,\omega_T)$, using the coefficient-passage internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The twist $\Lambda_T(1)$ is that of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

For $T=C,U,Z$, $D_T$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of $D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$ with itself, with its evaluation biduality $\delta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_TD_TK$. The smooth dualizing identifications are
$$\omega_C\cong\Lambda_C(1)[2],\qquad \omega_U\cong\Lambda_U(1)[2],\qquad \omega_Z\cong\Lambda_Z.$$
There are natural constructible comparison isomorphisms
$$j^*D_CK\cong D_Uj^*K,\qquad i^*D_CK\cong D_ZRi^!K,$$
where $Ri^!$ is the right adjoint to closed direct image in [prop-sf-localization-all-stages]. All these maps are represented by the corresponding finite-coefficient-field maps and commute with scalar extension. If the immersion pair is obtained by base change from a complementary pair $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$, $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ over $k_0$, they are maps of Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:Lg_C^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with the induced Weil structures on their source and target. Exactness and distinguished triangles refer to the underlying constructible categories; no triangulated structure on the category of Weil pairs is asserted.

source.place: Steps 2–3: smooth dualizing identifications, open restriction, biduality and closed-costalk comparison, with the stated perfect-field scope retained

proof.text: The base is now $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, exactly the datum required by [thm-coef-qbar-verdier]. The field is Noetherian, so $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every open subset of $C$ is quasi-compact; a finite cover by principal opens in finite-type affine charts shows that $U$ is finite type. The closed affine charts of $Z$ are quotients of those of $C$, so $Z$ is finite type as well. Restricting the closed diagonal of $C$ gives separatedness of $U$ and $Z$. These schemes are finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], and $\ell$ is invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] the PBC and derived-complete integral categories are the same full subcategories with the same reduction functors. Their raw localizations have the same objects and localized Hom groups by [def-weil-pbc-rational-category, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. The two pair definitions [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] use different scalar-extension functors, which agree only up to the completion comparisons; so the common-stage categories are not literally equal. [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] applies to $T=C,U,Z$ (noetherian, finite-dimensional, $\ell$ invertible). It gives the canonical exact $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linear equivalence $J_T$, the identity on integral objects, compatible with the finite stages, shifts, triangles and the geometric-Frobenius pullbacks, hence with Weil pairs. This is the identification asserted in the statement, and statements about either category are transported along it. Since the raw localization adds no objects, every finite-stage object has an integral representative, as rational purity requires.

source.place: Steps 2–3: domains and identification of the two common-stage coefficient conventions

proof.text:
Apply [thm-coef-qbar-verdier] to $C$, $U$ and $Z$, which are separated finite-type schemes over its fixed $k$. It supplies the exact contravariant dualities, their evaluation bidualities $\delta$, and their internal-Hom descriptions with $\omega_T=Ra_T^!\Lambda$. It also supplies, for each separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ among these schemes, the natural coefficient-passage comparison
$$\kappa_{f,K}:Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Xf^*D_YK.$$
This is already a statement in the common-stage constructible category, with its finite scalar-extension compatibility. For $f=i$, [prop-sf-localization-all-stages](2) identifies this exceptional inverse image with the right adjoint to closed direct image used in the statement.

source.place: Steps 2–3: exact duality, biduality and the constructible exceptional comparison

proof.text: The open subscheme $U$ inherits smoothness and relative dimension one from $C$: local finite presentations restrict to the same principal affine charts, and a map from a nilpotent thickening whose reduction lands in $U$ still lands in $U$, since the underlying spaces of a nilpotent thickening agree. Thus the infinitesimal lifting definition [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] restricts to $U$. By [lem-a1-reduced-boundary-smooth], $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth of pure relative dimension zero, since $k$ is perfect. Apply [cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes] in dimensions one, one and zero to $C,U,Z$. This gives the three asserted dualizing identifications, with the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]; the zero twist and shift are identities. The empty boundary satisfies the dimension-zero convention and all its objects are zero.

source.place: Step 2: the dualizing objects on C, U and the reduced boundary Z

proof.text:
The open immersion $j$ is smooth of relative dimension zero in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. It is locally of finite presentation, being locally an isomorphism onto principal opens. It is formally smooth by the argument of Step 3: a map $T\to U$ with $T\subset T'$ a first-order thickening over $C$ lifts uniquely, because $T'\to C$ lands in $U$ (same underlying space). Its nonempty fibres are single reduced points, of dimension zero. (The lemma that open immersions are etale uses the flat-unramified definition of etale, which is not the definition used here, so it is not used.) Its quasi-compactness was checked in Step 1, and it is separated. Apply [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] to $j$ in dimension zero; the integral presentation required there exists by Step 1. Its natural common-stage map is $\gamma_{j,K}:j^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj^!K$. Compose it with Step 2 to obtain
$$h_K=\kappa_{j,K}\circ\gamma_{j,K}:j^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Uj^*D_CK.$$
For $A=j^*D_CK$, define
$$\beta_{j,K}=D_U(h_K)\circ\delta_A:A\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Uj^*K.$$
Every factor is an isomorphism. Naturality of $\gamma$, $\kappa$ and biduality proves naturality of this composite. This establishes the open comparison entirely within the coefficient-passage categories, without applying an ordinary ringed-site lemma to a rationalized category.

source.place: Step 2: open restriction commutes with duality; use the existing common-stage exceptional formula and dimension-zero purity

proof.text:
Take $f=i$ in Step 2. For $A=i^*D_CK$ the natural comparison is
$$\kappa_{i,K}:Ri^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_ZA.$$
Dualizing and using the biduality of [thm-coef-qbar-verdier] gives the explicitly directed composite
$$\beta_{i,K}=D_Z(\kappa_{i,K})\circ\delta_A:i^*D_CK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_ZRi^!K.$$
This proves the closed comparison and its naturality. Equivalently, replace $K$ by $D_CK$ in the same exceptional formula and cancel $D_C^2$; this gives $Ri^!D_CK\cong D_Zi^*K$, the closed-costalk formula used in blueprint Step 3. No identification of an ambient ringed-site adjoint with a rationalized adjoint is assumed.

source.place: Step 3: closed-costalk duality followed by the two bidualities

proof.text: The maps $\kappa$ and $\delta$ are the finite-stage maps descended by [thm-coef-qbar-verdier], and $\gamma_j$ and the smooth dualizing orientations are the coefficient-passage maps of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. Both cited statements give finite scalar-extension compatibility. Applying duality, composing, and inverting these compatible isomorphisms preserves their compatibility squares. Consequently the displayed $\beta_j$ and $\beta_i$ are represented by exactly the same formulas at a finite coefficient field and commute with extension of that field; the inverse equations remain inverse equations in the pair category. This proves the coefficient clause without a new transport assertion.

source.place: Steps 2–3: finite-stage representatives and scalar extension

proof.text: Suppose the immersion pair descends over $k_0$ and $K$ carries its rational Weil isomorphism. By [cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance], duality, evaluation, biduality, the exceptional adjunction and the scalar comparisons lift to Weil pairs. The ordinary operation comparisons and exchange maps are equivariant by [lem-fix-weil-operations]. In particular the canonical comparison $\kappa$ of Step 2, obtained by transposing the evaluation/adjunction comparison, is equivariant: the equivariant adjunction bijection carries the same equivariant evaluation composite to its transpose. For the geometric orientations use the separate [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace], applied to $a_C,a_U,a_Z$ and to $j$; it gives equivariance of the dualizing identifications and of $\gamma_j$, including the prescribed Tate action. The formulas for $\beta_j$ and $\beta_i$ in Steps 4–5 use only these equivariant maps, their duals and biduality; composing their equivariance squares proves both formulas are morphisms of Weil pairs. The argument uses the rational Frobenius isomorphism itself, with no Frobenius-stable integral lattice.

source.place: Steps 2–3: Weil structures and equivariance of the actual comparisons and orientations

proof_origin.place: Steps 2–3; the same duality/purity argument is written using the existing common-stage exceptional formula to avoid unsupported ringed-site transport
